A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, algorithms, Figure 1, references, and appendices A–C. Content can be matched reliably despite repagination.

before.justification: v1 presents algorithms, theoretical guarantees, and proofs, including in the appendices. Figure 1 illustrates Gaussian cluster-assignment boundaries; it does not report an empirical evaluation.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical treatment and illustrative Figure 1. Neither its main text nor appendices report original experimental, simulation, user-study, or data-analysis results.

M1.justification: The cover tolerance in Section 4.2 changes from 1/T in v1 Algorithm 1 to 1/T′ in v2 Algorithm 2, where T′ is the initial sampling period. This revises a procedural parameter; the two-stage method and appendix subroutines otherwise remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version reports dataset-based evaluation. The online calibration problem and the Gaussian and exponential-family mixture settings considered theoretically are unchanged.

E2.justification: No empirical comparison methods are added or removed. The theoretical comparisons with cluster-then-predict and its constituent clustering and calibration algorithms remain the same.

E3.justification: Neither version introduces experimental splits, training budgets, evaluation procedures, or other empirical protocols. The cover-tolerance revision specifies the proposed algorithm, rather than an evaluation setting.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, sensitivity tests, robustness evaluations, or error analyses. Figure 1 and the analytical treatment of different mixture conditions are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated runs, seeds, empirical confidence intervals, or significance tests. The probability bounds in the theoretical guarantees are unchanged.

E6.justification: No empirical result entries are added, removed, or revised. Figure 1 is identical, and the stated O(T^1/2) versus O(T^2/3) theoretical rates remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions, theorem statements, and derivations, including appendices A–C, are retained apart from algorithm cross-reference updates. The cover-tolerance edit is not accompanied by a revised proof or bound.

C1.justification: Both versions claim discriminant and likelihood subgroup guarantees, faster calibration through a multi-objective approach, and separation-independent guarantees that can be easier to obtain than learning the clusters. The abstract and contribution scope are unchanged.

C2.justification: The normative qualifications in Section 1.1, interpretation of the clustering-versus-calibration gap, and applicability discussion in Section 5 remain unchanged. No substantive limitation or mechanism explanation is added.

D1.justification: The documented cover-resolution parameter changes from 1/T to 1/T′, affecting how the pseudocode is instantiated. However, the explanation preceding the proof of Theorem 4.3 still specifies 1/T. Other technical details and resource-access information are unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 1.3 replaces a broken citation with explicit attribution to Gupta et al. (2022) alongside Haghtalab et al. (2023) as online-multicalibration building blocks. Gupta et al. already appeared elsewhere; the bibliography and broader research positioning are unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 makes small wording and punctuation corrections, repairs a citation, and updates algorithm numbering and cross-references. Section order, explanations, and the main-text/appendix organization remain essentially identical.

P2.justification: Reduced vertical margins change page breaks and content placement. The existing DCE cluster-then-predict box gains the label Algorithm 1, shifting subsequent algorithm numbers. Figure 1 retains the same panels and caption; no figures or tables are added.

improvement.justification: Citation and numbering repairs improve attribution and navigation. However, v1 consistently specifies a 1/T cover, whereas v2 changes the algorithm box to 1/T′ while retaining 1/T in its explanation. The unchanged proofs do not explain this discrepancy. These limited editorial benefits and the new specification ambiguity leave the net quality direction uncertain.
